title: Parkinson-related factors influencing the ability of optimal biofilm control
summary:
The aim of the planned study is to compare the tooth brushing process of people with Parkinson's disease with the tooth brushing process of people without a diagnosed neurodegenerative disease. In addition, the study will investigate whether the removal of dental plaque - also known as plaque or biofilm - in people with Parkinson's disease can be improved by the use of an electric toothbrush compared to a manual toothbrush.  
As a benefit for science and the future care of patients, it is expected to be able to characterize the limitations of Parkinson's disease in oral hygiene at home and to find out whether an electric toothbrush is more effective than a manual toothbrush and to find out whether an electric toothbrush has a positive effect on the oral hygiene of patients with Parkinson's disease.
A video recording of the participants brushing their teeth is made, which is later analyzed to find out whether there are differences between the brushing movements of healthy people and people with Parkinson's disease.
The participants with Parkinson's disease then continue and are alternately given both types of toothbrush (commercially available electric or manual) for a brushing phase of 4 weeks each.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Parkinson's disease diagnosis with akinetic-rigid type (n=40), specialist diagnosis
- Höhn and Yahr>=2 
- healthy control subjects (n=40) without neurodegenerative diseases 
- Regular use of a manual toothbrush for self-performed oral hygiene at home
- ≥ 10 natural teeth 
- Interest and consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Preexisting conditions that have a direct impact on manual dexterity (e.g. hemiparesis, pronounced arthrosis, gout on the upper extremities)  
- rejection of oscillating electric toothbrushes or electronic aids for self-performed oral hygiene  
- Höhn&Yahr 5 
- Dementia (MOCA-instrument)
